items.why: avoid는 동명사를 취하므로 to eat를 eating으로 고쳐야 해요.

items.q: Choose the part that must be corrected: My brother is good at to cook pasta.
items.why: 전치사 at 뒤에는 동명사가 와야 하므로 to cook을 cooking으로 고쳐야 해요.

items.q: Choose the part that must be corrected: We decided taking a taxi because it was raining.
items.why: decide는 to부정사를 취하므로 taking을 to take로 고쳐야 해요.

items.q: Choose the part that must be corrected: I'm looking forward to see my grandparents next week.
items.why: look forward to의 to는 전치사이므로 to see를 seeing으로 고쳐야 해요.

items.q: Choose the part that must be corrected: Mina promised being on time.
items.why: promise는 to부정사를 취하므로 being을 to be로 고쳐야 해요.

items.q: Choose the part that must be corrected: They were too excited sleeping last night.
items.why: too + 형용사 + to V 구문이므로 sleeping을 to sleep으로 고쳐야 해요.

items.q: Choose the part that must be corrected: My teacher let us to use dictionaries during the test.
items.why: 사역동사 let 뒤에는 동사원형을 써야 하므로 to use를 use로 고쳐야 해요.

items.q: Choose the part that must be corrected: Thank you for to invite me to your party.
items.why: 전치사 for 뒤에는 동명사가 와야 하므로 to invite를 inviting으로 고쳐야 해요.

items.q: Choose the part that must be corrected: Jisu wants learning how to swim this summer.
items.why: want는 to부정사를 취하므로 learning을 to learn으로 고쳐야 해요.

items.q: Choose the part that must be corrected: Do you mind to close the door?
items.why: mind는 동명사를 취하므로 to close를 closing으로 고쳐야 해요.

items.q: Which sentence has the same meaning as ‘He is so tired that he can't walk.’?
o: He is tired enough to walk.
He is too tired to walk.
He is so tired to walk.
items.why: too ... to V는 '너무 ~해서 ...할 수 없다'는 뜻이라 so ... that ... can't와 같아요.

items.q: ‘She went to the clinic to see the doctor.’에서 to see의 의미로 알맞은 것은?
items.why: to see the doctor는 병원에 간 목적(~을 보기 위해서)을 나타내요.

items.q: ‘My dream is to become a pilot.’에서 to become a pilot의 문장 성분은?
items.why: to become a pilot은 be동사 뒤에서 주어 My dream을 설명하는 보어 역할을 해요.

items.q: Which sentence uses a gerund as the subject?
items.why: Swimming이 문장의 주어 자리에 쓰인 동명사예요.

items.q: ‘It is fun to learn new words.’에서 It의 역할로 알맞은 것은?
items.why: It은 가주어이고 진짜 주어(진주어)는 to learn new words예요.

items.q:
A: Why did you go to the bookstore?
B: ___ a gift for my sister.
items.why: 이유(목적)를 말할 때 to부정사를 써요.

items.q:
A: What do you hope to do this winter?
B: I hope ___ snowboarding.
items.why: hope는 to부정사를 목적어로 취해요.

items.q:
A: Did you finish your report?
B: Not yet. I need two more hours ___ it.
items.why: 시간 뒤에서 '~하기 위한'의 뜻으로 to부정사를 써요.

items.title: A New Hobby
items.text: Last spring, Jina decided to start running. She had never enjoyed exercising, but her doctor advised her to move more. At first, she could not run for even five minutes without stopping to rest. Her friend Hana suggested keeping a small notebook to record each day. Jina refused to give up, and she wrote down every run. After two months, she finished running three kilometers without stopping. Now she looks forward to jogging every morning, and she has even started helping her little brother train for his school race.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: Why Jina's doctor told her to stop exercising
How Hana trained for a school race last year
How Jina turned running into a habit
Where Jina bought her first pair of running shoes
qs.why: Jina starts running, keeps a notebook, and improves until she enjoys it. 중심 내용은 달리기 습관 만들기예요.

qs.q: Why did Jina begin running?
o: Her doctor told her to be more active.
Her friend Hana asked her to join a school team.
She wanted to win a race against her brother.
She had always loved sports since she was a child.
qs.why: 본문: her doctor advised her to move more.

qs.q: What did Hana suggest?
o: Running only on the weekends with her brother
Resting for a week after every long run
Practicing at a track near her school
Writing down each run in a notebook
qs.why: 본문: Hana suggested keeping a small notebook to record each day.

qs.q: What can we infer about Jina now?
o: She plans to stop running when summer comes.
She has become more positive about exercise.
She still cannot run for more than five minutes.
She dislikes helping other people with sports.
qs.why: 아침마다 조깅을 기대하고 동생을 돕는 모습에서 운동에 긍정적으로 바뀌었음을 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: Which statement is true?
o: Jina ran three kilometers on her very first day.
Jina's little brother taught her how to run.
Jina can run three kilometers without stopping now.
Jina stopped recording her runs after a week.
qs.why: 본문: After two months, she finished running three kilometers without stopping.

items.title: The Class Garden
items.text: Our class decided to make a small garden behind the school. First, we asked our science teacher to help us choose the right place. She told us to look for a spot with a lot of sunlight. Then we spent two weekends digging the soil and planting tomatoes, beans, and herbs. Some students were afraid of touching worms, but they soon learned that worms help plants grow. Now we take turns watering the garden before class. Last week, we picked our first tomatoes and shared them at lunch. Everyone agreed that working together was the best part.

qs.q: What is the best title for the passage?
o: A Science Test About Worms and Beans
How One Student Won a Cooking Contest
Why Schools Should Sell Fresh Tomatoes
qs.why: 학급 친구들이 함께 텃밭을 만드는 이야기예요.

qs.q: What did the students do on two weekends?
o: They visited a farm and bought some tomatoes.
They built a fence around the school building.
They listened to their teacher talk about worms.
They dug the soil and planted vegetables and herbs.
qs.why: 본문: we spent two weekends digging the soil and planting...

qs.q: In the passage, “take turns” means to ___.
o: do something all at the same time
stop doing something for a while
ask a teacher to do something
qs.why: take turns는 '교대로 하다'라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Who does “they” in “they soon learned” refer to?
o: The science teacher and her class
The tomatoes and the beans in the garden
Some students who were afraid of worms
Everyone who shared lunch last week
qs.why: they는 바로 앞 문장의 Some students를 가리켜요.

qs.q: Which statement is true?
o: The class planted flowers instead of vegetables.
The class has already picked some tomatoes.
The teacher chose a spot without much sun.
The students watered the garden after class.
qs.why: 본문: Last week, we picked our first tomatoes.

items.title: A Day at the Market
items.text: On Saturday, my family went to the old market near our town. My father wanted to buy fresh fish, and my mother needed to find some cheap vegetables. I did not enjoy walking in the crowd at first, but then I smelled something delicious. A woman was selling hot rice cakes, so I stopped to buy some. She smiled and gave me an extra one for free. My little sister kept asking to try everything. In the end, we spent three hours there and went home with heavy bags and happy faces.

qs.q: Why did the writer stop at the rice cake stand?
o: To buy some hot rice cakes
To ask the woman where the fish was sold
To rest because the bags were too heavy
To meet a friend who worked at the market
qs.why: 본문: I stopped to buy some. to buy는 멈춘 목적이에요.

qs.q: What did the woman do for the writer?
o: She carried the writer's heavy bags.
She showed the family the way out.
She gave an extra rice cake for free.
She taught the writer how to cook.
qs.why: 본문: gave me an extra one for free.

qs.q: How did the writer feel at the end of the day?
o: Tired and angry at the crowd
qs.why: heavy bags and happy faces에서 즐거운 하루였음을 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: In the passage, “in the end” means ___.
qs.why: in the end는 '결국, 마침내'라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What did the writer's mother need to find?
o: A gift for her youngest daughter
Fresh fish for dinner that night
A warm coat for the cold season
qs.why: 본문: my mother needed to find some cheap vegetables.

items.title: Learning to Code
items.text: Min-jun joined the school coding club because he wanted to make his own game. At first, he had trouble understanding even simple commands, and he nearly gave up. His teacher, Ms. Choi, told him not to worry about mistakes. “Every programmer makes errors,” she said. “The important thing is finding them and fixing them.” After that, Min-jun began testing his code after every few lines. It took him a month to finish a small game about a jumping cat. He was proud of it, and now he enjoys teaching new members how to start.

qs.q: Why did Ms. Choi say, “Every programmer makes errors”?
o: To warn Min-jun about a hard exam
To explain why the club was closing
To encourage Min-jun not to lose hope
To blame Min-jun for his careless code
qs.why: 실수는 누구나 한다는 말로 민준이를 격려하려는 의도예요.

qs.q: How long did it take Min-jun to finish the game?
qs.why: 본문: It took him a month to finish a small game.

qs.q: In the passage, “gave up” means ___.
qs.why: nearly gave up은 '거의 포기할 뻔했다'는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What changed Min-jun's way of coding?
o: He stopped using the school computers.
He wrote longer programs without any rest.
He copied the games of other members.
He started testing his code after every few lines.
qs.why: 격려를 들은 뒤 몇 줄마다 코드를 시험해 보기 시작했어요.

qs.q: What can we infer about Min-jun now?
o: He feels confident enough to help others.
He thinks coding is too difficult for him.
He wants to leave the club soon.
He has never made a mistake in his code.
qs.why: 신입 회원을 가르치는 것을 즐기는 모습에서 자신감을 알 수 있어요.

items.title: Helping Sea Turtles
items.text: Every summer, volunteers visit a quiet beach to protect baby sea turtles. Before the eggs hatch, they put a small fence around the nests to keep animals away. When night comes, the volunteers must avoid using bright lights, because the little turtles may follow the light instead of going to the sea. Some tourists forget to turn off their flashlights, so the volunteers politely ask them to do it. Thanks to this work, more baby turtles can reach the water safely. The volunteers hope to make the beach a safe home for turtles for many years.

qs.q: Why must the volunteers avoid bright lights at night?
o: Bright lights make the eggs too hot to hatch.
Baby turtles may follow the light away from the sea.
Tourists cannot sleep when the beach is bright.
The fence around the nests might break.
qs.why: 본문: the little turtles may follow the light instead of going to the sea.

qs.q: What do the volunteers ask some tourists to do?
qs.why: 본문: volunteers politely ask them to turn off flashlights.

qs.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: Volunteers work to keep baby sea turtles safe.
Tourists are the only people who love turtles.
Sea turtles lay their eggs in many different seasons.
A beach should be closed to visitors forever.
qs.why: 자원봉사자들이 아기 바다거북을 보호하는 활동이 중심 내용이에요.

qs.q: In the passage, “hatch” means ___.
o: to come out of an egg
qs.why: hatch는 '(알이) 부화하다'라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Which statement is true?
o: The volunteers visit the beach only in winter.
The volunteers put a fence around the nests.
The tourists put the fence around the nests.
The volunteers use bright lights at night.
qs.why: 본문: they put a small fence around the nests.

items.title: Kimjang Day
items.text: In late autumn, my grandmother's house is full of people. It is the day for making kimchi for the winter. My aunts begin washing cabbages early in the morning, and my uncles carry them to the yard. My grandmother does not like using too much salt, so she checks every cabbage herself. I am too young to make the sauce, but she lets me spread it on the leaves. Our hands become red and sticky, and we laugh a lot. By evening, we have more than fifty boxes. Grandmother says that kimchi tastes better when many people make it together.

qs.q: Why doesn't the writer make the sauce?
o: The writer has to wash the cabbages.
The writer's hands are too sticky.
The writer is too young to do it.
qs.why: 본문: I am too young to make the sauce.

qs.q: What does the writer's grandmother care about?
qs.why: 그녀는 소금을 많이 쓰지 않으려고 배추를 일일이 확인해요. 맛을 중시한다고 볼 수 있어요.

qs.q: What does “it” refer to in the last sentence?
qs.why: tastes better when many people make it에서 it은 kimchi를 가리켜요.

qs.q: What is the mood of the day?
qs.why: 많은 사람이 모여 웃으며 일하는 즐겁고 바쁜 분위기예요.

qs.q: Which statement is true?
o: The family makes more than fifty boxes of kimchi.
The uncles wash all the cabbages.
The writer makes all the sauce alone.
qs.why: 본문: By evening, we have more than fifty boxes.

items.title: A Kind Neighbor
items.text: Mr. Han lives alone on the third floor of our building, and the elevator is often broken. Last Tuesday, I saw him carrying two heavy bags up the stairs. He stopped on every floor to rest. I felt worried, so I offered to help him. At first he refused to let me carry the bags, but then he smiled and handed me one. When we reached his door, he thanked me for being so kind and gave me an orange. Since then, I have tried to say hello whenever I see him. Helping others can make an ordinary day feel special.

qs.q: Why did Mr. Han stop on every floor?
o: He wanted to say hello to his neighbors.
He was tired from carrying heavy bags.
He was waiting for the elevator to work.
He had forgotten which floor he lived on.
qs.why: 무거운 가방을 들고 계단을 올라서 쉬어야 했다고 추론할 수 있어요.

qs.q: What did the writer do when feeling worried?
qs.why: 본문: I felt worried, so I offered to help him.

qs.q: What did Mr. Han do at the end?
o: He thanked the writer and gave an orange.
He refused the help again and went inside.
He asked the writer to fix the elevator.
He carried the writer's bags upstairs.
qs.why: 본문: he thanked me ... and gave me an orange.

qs.q: In the passage, “handed” means ___.
qs.why: handed me one은 '나에게 하나를 건네주었다'는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What is the writer's message in the last sentence?
o: Elevators should be repaired every week.
Small acts of kindness can make a day special.
Old people should live on the first floor.
qs.why: 마지막 문장은 남을 돕는 작은 행동의 가치를 말하고 있어요.

items.title: Cooking Without a Recipe
items.text: My uncle never uses a recipe when he cooks. He says that following every step makes him bored. Instead, he tastes the food again and again and adds a little salt or sugar. Last night, he made a vegetable soup for our family. I was worried because he forgot to buy onions, but he used extra carrots and it tasted great. “Cooking is like drawing,” he told me. “You should not be afraid of making mistakes.” I still prefer to follow a recipe, but I am learning to trust my taste a little more.

qs.q: What did the uncle do when he had no onions?
o: He went out to buy some more.
He asked the writer to cook.
qs.why: 본문: he used extra carrots and it tasted great.

qs.q: What does the uncle mean by “Cooking is like drawing”?
o: You can try freely and learn from mistakes
You must follow each line exactly
You need special tools to start
You should cook only for your family
qs.why: 그림처럼 요리도 자유롭게 시도하고 실수를 두려워하지 말라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: How is the writer different from the uncle?
o: The writer never tastes the food.
The writer likes following a recipe.
qs.why: 본문: I still prefer to follow a recipe.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: A recipe for a vegetable soup
A family trip to buy onions
An uncle's free way of cooking
qs.why: 레시피 없이 요리하는 삼촌의 방식과 그에 대한 글쓴이의 생각이 중심이에요.

items.title: Sleeping Better
items.text: Many teenagers go to bed late and feel tired the next day. Experts say that avoiding screens for an hour before bed can help you fall asleep faster. It is also a good idea to keep your room dark and cool. Some students like reading a paper book instead of watching videos. Others try to write down tomorrow's plans so that they can stop worrying. Of course, you cannot change everything in one night. Start by choosing one habit and keeping it for a week. Small changes are easier to continue, and soon you may wake up feeling much better.

qs.q: What is the writer's purpose?
o: To give advice about better sleep
To sell a new type of bed
To tell a story about a tired student
To explain how screens are made
qs.why: 잠을 잘 자는 방법에 대한 조언을 주는 글이에요.

qs.q: Which is NOT suggested in the passage?
o: Keeping the bedroom dark and cool
Reading a paper book before bed
qs.why: 따뜻한 우유는 언급되지 않았어요.

qs.q: How long should we avoid screens before bed?
qs.why: 본문: avoiding screens for an hour before bed.

qs.q: What does the writer advise at the end?
o: Change every habit on the first night.
Go to bed at midnight every day.
Choose one habit and keep it for a week.
qs.why: 본문: Start by choosing one habit and keeping it for a week.

qs.q: In the passage, “habit” means ___.
qs.why: habit은 '습관'이라는 뜻이에요.

items.title: A Letter to Jake
items.text: Dear Jake, Thank you for your last letter! I was happy to hear that you finally started learning Korean. I am writing to tell you about my summer plan. I hope to visit your city in August if my parents agree. I am really looking forward to seeing the clock tower you told me about. Would you mind showing me around? I am also planning to bring some snacks from Korea for your family. Please write back soon and tell me what you want to eat or do. Your friend, Somin

qs.q: Why did Somin write this letter?
o: To say sorry for not writing back earlier
To share her travel plan and ask for his help
To invite Jake to a party in her city
To complain about her summer homework
qs.why: 여행 계획을 알리고 안내를 부탁하려는 목적이에요.

qs.q: What does Somin plan to bring for Jake's family?
qs.why: 본문: I am also planning to bring some snacks from Korea.

qs.q: What can we infer about Somin's trip?
o: She has already bought the tickets.
She will travel with Jake's parents.
She plans to stay for a whole year.
It is not completely decided yet.
qs.why: if my parents agree라는 표현에서 아직 확정되지 않았음을 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: In the letter, “show me around” means ___.
qs.why: show someone around는 '~에게 곳곳을 안내해 주다'라는 뜻이에요.

items.ex: You should avoid eating too much sugar.
items.exko: 너는 설탕을 너무 많이 먹는 것을 피해야 해요.

items.ex: She will refuse to sign the paper.
items.exko: 그녀는 그 서류에 서명하기를 거절할 거예요.

items.ex: I suggest taking a short break.
